## León: The Old and New City

### León, Nicaragua's Former Capital

León was once the country's capital. In 1609, an earthquake and the subsequent eruption of Momotombo volcano destroyed the old city. Its ruins can still be seen today.

## León: A City of Museums and Churches

The new city of León lies 30 km from the old one. Its principal landmark is the Cathedral of the Assumption, the largest cathedral in Central America, home to Antonio Sarria's remarkable painting "The Descent from the Cross" and the tomb of poet Rubén Darío. Other highlights include the Insurreccional Luis Toruño Charata Museum, an Arts Center with an extensive collection of 18th-century religious paintings and pre-Columbian ceramics, the Rubén Darío Museum, the Museum of Legends and Traditions, the Gallery of Heroes and Martyrs, the Adicat Museum, and beautiful colonial churches: 18 churches spanning a wide range of architectural styles. Nearby Chinandega is described as the country's hottest place and the birthplace of its finest rum.

## The White City and Dry Tropical Landscapes: What to See in Liberia, Costa Rica

One of Costa Rica's historic cities, Liberia long served as a trading center for Guanacaste Province. Its nickname, the "White City," comes from the whitewashed houses built during the colonial era.

## National Parks and Beaches on Trips from Liberia

The city is a departure point for visits to national parks and some of the country's most beautiful beaches. Excursions head to Rincón de la Vieja volcano, Santa Rosa National Park, and the beaches of Nicoya.

Costa Ricans call Liberia the "White City" because of its many white colonial-style buildings. Spanish culture and traditions, including the siesta, have been preserved here to a greater extent than in many other cities in the country. One of its main landmarks is the imposing Cathedral of the Immaculate Conception. Liberia is also a starting point for exploring Costa Rica's protected natural areas, particularly Rincón de la Vieja National Park, with its waterfalls and scenic volcanoes.

## A Wide Range of Activities in Liberia

The city has a beautiful park and many restaurants. Tourist infrastructure is well developed, with numerous car-rental outlets. Liberia also has an international airport.

Lima was founded by Francisco Pizarro in 1535 and later became the capital of independent Peru. A first visit usually begins in the historic center and Plaza Mayor.

Among the historic landmarks are the Archbishop's Palace, Casa Aliaga, the Government Palace, the Cathedral, and other monuments of the colonial period. The Larco Museum is a particular highlight.

Continue into modern Lima with Miraflores, Love Park, and the Bridge of Sighs. Huaca Pucllana and the Pachacamac archaeological complex reveal an earlier chapter of Peru's history.

Fishing on the Limay is also a way to experience Patagonia's river landscapes: clear water, pebble banks, pools, and fast-flowing stretches. The itinerary with accommodation at Lakeshore Chalet dedicates five full days to the river.

Guides choose the fishing stretch and approach according to water levels and fish movements. The itinerary names rainbow and brown trout, with dry flies, nymphing, and streamers among the methods used. Visiting different stretches offers varied fishing conditions along the same river.

The Limay is among the fishing rivers of Nahuel Huapi National Park. A permit is required to fish. Check the conditions of your chosen trip for included services, licenses, and equipment.
